name: Hematopoiesis
summary: One hematopoietic stem cell (CD34⁺) makes every blood cell. The common myeloid progenitor gives red cells (EPO), platelets (TPO, via megakaryocytes), granulocytes (G-CSF; IL-5 for eosinophils), monocytes and macrophages (M-CSF) and mast cells; the common lymphoid progenitor (IL-7) gives B cells, T cells (matured in the thymus) and NK cells (IL-15). Drugs that mimic the signals: epoetin, filgrastim (G-CSF), sargramostim (GM-CSF), romiplostim and eltrombopag (TPO).
tissue: bone marrow (adults: axial skeleton; fetus: yolk sac, then liver and spleen, then marrow — “Young Liver Synthesizes Blood”)

hsc.name: Hematopoietic stem cell
hsc.notes: CD34⁺. Self-renews and makes every blood cell. Lives in the bone marrow niche; mobilized into blood by G-CSF (and plerixafor) for stem cell transplant collection.

cmp.name: Common myeloid progenitor
cmp.notes: Gives red cells, platelets, granulocytes, monocytes (and mast cells). Its malignant clones: myeloproliferative neoplasms (CML, polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, myelofibrosis) and AML.

clp.name: Common lymphoid progenitor
clp.notes: Gives B cells, T cells and NK cells. Its malignant clones: ALL and lymphomas.

rbc.name: Erythrocyte
rbc.notes: Via proerythroblasts, normoblasts (nucleus expelled) and reticulocytes (a day in blood, RNA still in them). Lives about 120 days; no mitochondria, so glycolysis only (2,3-BPG). Reticulocyte count shows marrow response.

mk.name: Megakaryocyte
mk.notes: Huge, polyploid marrow cell that sheds platelets from its cytoplasm.

plt.name: Platelets
plt.notes: Anucleate fragments; live 8–10 days, a third held in the spleen. Granules: dense (ADP, Ca²⁺, serotonin) and α (vWF, fibrinogen, fibronectin, PF4). GPIb binds vWF (Bernard-Soulier when missing); GPIIb/IIIa binds fibrinogen (Glanzmann).

mb.name: Myeloblast
mb.notes: First of the granulocyte line; Auer rods in AML.

neut.name: Neutrophil
neut.notes: Most numerous leukocyte; acute inflammation and bacteria. Multilobed nucleus (hypersegmented in B12/folate deficiency); band forms in infection. Granules: myeloperoxidase, lysozyme, alkaline phosphatase. Drawn by IL-8, C5a, LTB₄, kallikrein.

eos.name: Eosinophil
eos.notes: Bilobed, red-orange granules (major basic protein): helminths and allergy. Raised by “PACCMAN”: parasites, asthma, chronic adrenal insufficiency, Churg-Strauss, myeloproliferative disorders, allergy, neoplasia.

baso.name: Basophil
baso.notes: Rarest leukocyte; dark granules with heparin and histamine, makes leukotrienes. Basophilia suggests a myeloproliferative neoplasm (CML).

mono.name: Monocyte
mono.notes: Kidney-bean nucleus; in blood 1–3 days, then into tissue as a macrophage or dendritic cell.

mac.name: Macrophage
mac.notes: Phagocytes and antigen presenters (MHC II), named by tissue: Kupffer cells (liver), microglia (brain), alveolar macrophages, osteoclasts (bone), Langerhans cells are dendritic. Activated by IFN-γ; make IL-1, IL-6, IL-8, IL-12, TNF-α.

mast.name: Mast cell
mast.notes: Tissue cell (from a myeloid precursor); IgE on FcεRI cross-linked by antigen releases histamine, heparin, tryptase: type I hypersensitivity. Cromolyn stabilizes it.

bcell.name: B cell
bcell.notes: Matures in the bone marrow (central tolerance there); humoral immunity. CD19, CD20, CD21 (EBV receptor). Becomes a plasma cell or memory B cell.

plasma.name: Plasma cell
plasma.notes: Makes large amounts of one antibody; clock-face chromatin, perinuclear halo (Golgi). Multiple myeloma is its cancer.

tcell.name: T cell
tcell.notes: Leaves the marrow as a progenitor and matures in the thymus: positive selection (cortex, MHC binding) then negative selection (medulla, AIRE, self). CD3. DiGeorge syndrome: no thymus, no T cells.

cd4.name: CD4⁺ helper T cell
cd4.notes: Sees MHC II; becomes Th1, Th2, Th17, Treg or Tfh (see Helper T cell differentiation). HIV infects it.

cd8.name: CD8⁺ cytotoxic T cell
cd8.notes: Sees MHC I; kills infected and tumor cells with perforin and granzymes, or Fas ligand.

nk.name: NK cell
nk.notes: Innate lymphocyte (CD16, CD56); kills cells that lack MHC I (missing self) and antibody-coated cells (ADCC). Activated by IL-2, IL-12, IL-15, IFN-α/β.

scf.name: SCF + IL-3
scf.notes: Stem cell factor (c-kit ligand) and IL-3 keep progenitors growing.

il7.name: IL-7
il7.notes: Lymphoid development, from the marrow stroma and thymus. IL-7 receptor α (and the common γ chain) defects: SCID.

epo.name: Erythropoietin
epo.notes: Made by peritubular interstitial cells of the kidney in response to hypoxia (HIF). Low in chronic kidney disease (anemia); high in hypoxia and from some tumors (renal cell carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma). Epoetin alfa replaces it; athletes abuse it.

tpo.name: Thrombopoietin
tpo.notes: Made by the liver. Romiplostim and eltrombopag (TPO receptor agonists) treat immune thrombocytopenia.

gcsf.name: G-CSF
gcsf.notes: Filgrastim (recombinant G-CSF) treats neutropenia after chemotherapy and mobilizes stem cells.

il5.name: IL-5
il5.notes: From Th2 cells; mepolizumab blocks it.

tissue.name: Enters tissue
tissue.notes: Monocytes leave the blood and mature into macrophages and dendritic cells in tissues.

shed.name: Platelet shedding
shed.notes: Megakaryocytes push out proplatelets that break into platelets in marrow sinusoids.

thymus.name: Thymus
thymus.notes: Maturation and selection in the thymus.

cd4sel.name: MHC II selection
cd4sel.notes: T cells whose TCR binds MHC II keep CD4.

cd8sel.name: MHC I selection
cd8sel.notes: T cells whose TCR binds MHC I keep CD8.

act.name: Antigen + T cell help
act.notes: Antigen on the B cell receptor plus help from a helper T cell (CD40L, cytokines).
